The peak pressure acting on the front wall after time $t_{c}$ is the algebraic sum of the peak incident shock pressure $P_{s}$ and the peak drag pressure, equal to the peak dynamic pressure q multiplied by the drag coefficient $C_{D}$ of the structure. This is shown in Equation 2-9.

The peak dynamic pressure is calculated based on $P_{s}$ using Figure 2-3 (+). The drag coefficient $C_{D}$ ,which gives the relationship between the dynamic pressure and the total translational pressure in the direction of the wind produced by the dynamic pressure,varies with the Mach number (or with the Reynold's number at low incident pressures)and the relative geometry of the structure. A value of $C_{D}=1$ for the front wall is considered adequate for the pressure ranges considered in this manual. At higher pressure ranges, the duration of the reflected pressure $t_{r f}$ may be less than the clearing time $t_{c}$ causing the above procedure to be inaccurate. Therefore, a second pressuretime curve must be constructed (dotted triangle as indicated in Figure 2-191a (+)) based on the reflected shock pressure without clearing using the total reflected pressure impulse $i_{r}$ from Figure 2-15 (+) (Figure 2-191a).
